subject: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — stabilization bridge
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — initial report

Samira —

We started seeing a large spike in 5xx error rates and a corresponding throughput surge on your production tenant starting ~07:55 PT. Short summary:

- Error rate: baseline ~0.4% -> peaked at 9.8% for ~12 minutes.
- Throughput: sustained 2.6x normal token/sec for the same window.
- Impact: degraded response completion for some short prompts and intermittent timeouts.

I'm attaching a short snapshot of the error logs and a traffic graph. We're running a roll-forward triage to confirm root cause, but initial telemetry points to an autoretry loop from the client combined with a rare KV cache eviction pattern that amplified load.

Immediate plan (what we're doing now):
- Throttle inferred retries at the gateway for your tenant (in progress).
- Enable fallback routing to a lower-latency, smaller model variant for low-priority routes (can flip in ~10–15m).
- Spin up burst capacity pool + increase request concurrency cap for your tenant.

We need to stand up a short stabilization bridge with your engineering and our on-call infra/serving leads. Marcus and Lauren are looped in. Can you confirm availability for a 30-min bridge now?

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189
Redwood Inference

Attachments: error_snapshot.log (text), traffic_graph.png (image)

From: Samira Patel <s.patel@medicore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Paul Gomez <paul.gomez@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:20:33 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — initial report

Ben — thanks for the rapid flag. We're seeing user-facing failures in our billing service and a backlog on our side. Paul and I can be on a bridge — we have people standing by.

Immediate ask: can you keep our traffic on the current model until we confirm client-side retry behavior? Switching models mid-window will complicate our diagnostics. If the retry loop is on our side, we'd prefer to throttle retries from our client.

I'll join if you open a bridge.

—Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Site Reliability, Medicore Health
s.patel@medicore.com

Attachment: medicore_error_sample.log (sent)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:28:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — request for stabilization bridge

Folks — forwarding Samira's reply. Customer prefers to avoid model switching initially; asks that we try gateway-level throttles and keep them on current model so they can run diagnostics. They're ready to join a bridge.

Can infra/serving do the following ASAP?
- Apply a tenant-level retry cap (2 retries) at the gateway (non-disruptive).
- Temporarily pin concurrency for the tenant to limit source amplification.
- Monitor KV cache eviction rates; if evictions spike, fallback to cached-optimized code path.

Marcus — do you want to own the bridge? I'll coordinate with the customer.

Ben

Attachments: medicore_error_sample.log (from customer)

- Lauren: customer communications and logging handoff; collect client-side retry patterns.

I will run the bridge and escalate to Eng leadership if metrics don't improve.

marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <s.patel@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:50:12 -0700
Subject: RE: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — mitigation steps applied

On Sun, Oct 11, 2026 at 08:35 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Opening a temporary exec/ops bridge now (30m) to stabilize plus an escalation channel.

Team — quick status update: applied tenant-level retry cap (max 2) at the gateway and enabled a soft concurrency pin that limits inflight requests per-tenant. Observed immediate impact: 5xx error rate dropped from 9.8% -> 1.1% over the first 6 minutes.

What we changed:
- Gateway retry caps (non-breaking) — rolled in 2 AZs first, rolling in remainder.
- Soft concurrency pins (limits not hard-fails) to reduce amplification.
- Telemetry: added high-frequency sampling for client's tenant to capture additional traces.

Next steps (on our side):
- Mina to add burst GPU nodes to reduce tail latency for remaining requests.
- If error rate does not fall below 0.5% in the next 15 minutes, we will propose a controlled model fallback with prior notice to Medicore.

Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: medicore_action_plan.docx (current mitigation brief)

From: Samira Patel <s.patel@medicore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — thanks, on bridge

Thanks — we saw immediate improvement on our side as well. 2 things:

1) We identified an aggressive client-side retry policy triggered by an upstream monitoring probe during a deploy — we're disabling that probe to prevent further amplification.
2) Can we get a short after-action note with timing for the changes and what telemetry you captured for our post-mortem?

We'll keep a small team on the bridge for 30 minutes and then stand down if things continue to look stable.

—Samira

Attachment: medicore_postmortem_notes-template.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@medicore.com>, Paul Gomez <paul.gomez@medicore.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: [Urgent] Medicore: throughput spike & error-rate — stabilization summary and next steps

Samira / Paul —

Quick summary of the bridge and actions (for your post-mortem):

Timeline:
- 07:55 PT: Customer-side monitoring probe triggered retries; tenant throughput amplifies.
- 08:12 PT: Redwood alerted and initial diagnostics started.
- 08:28 PT: Bridge requested; customer asked to avoid model switch.
- 08:35–08:50 PT: Gateway retry cap and soft concurrency pin applied; error rate reduced to ~1.1%.
- 09:00 PT: Medicore disabled the probe; tail errors continued to reduce.
- 13:20 PT: All telemetry shows steady-state error rate ~0.2% and normal throughput.

Actions taken by Redwood:
- Non-disruptive gateway retry cap (tenant-level).
- Temporary soft concurrency pin to reduce amplification.
- Burst GPU pool provisioned to reduce tail latency while traces collected.
- High-frequency sampling of traces for the tenant; attaching the snapshot and action log.

Attachments: error_snapshot.log, traffic_graph.png, medicore_action_plan.docx

Open items / recommendations:
- Medicore to keep retry policy conservative for probes and background jobs.
- We'll deliver a short after-action doc with captured traces and recommended limits by EOD.
- Recommend a follow-up meeting with Platform + Medicore SRE on Monday to review rollout-safe limits and failover policies.

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

If anything regresses, I will escalate immediately to Marcus and the execs.
